name: fx_bat9
doc: Stands in for saves/battle_re/bat9_lake.state (the Diablos fight in the Cathedral's inner hall, loc 082, Crono's command menu up). From cathedral_hall with the party the owner's game brought there poked in first -- the sheet bytes that game's own fights left (Crono 34/83 HP, 2 MP and his experience bytes, Lucca 48/75 HP, Marle's HP), the bag (Pendant, Heal), 925 G, the persistent RNG cursor $29AD = 86, the records $29B0-$2A1F those fights' ends left (C1 writes them at a battle's end, CF:FC5B/FC69; the capture's carry the Diablos, id 48, of an earlier fight) and the play clock (8:42:12, so that it reads the capture's 8:42:18 here). A recipe cannot replay that history. Then the owner's own route, read off the capture's follower ring ($7F:0C00-0DFF, head $01AB = 6F: every move the lead made since the hall loaded, its velocity and the pad's pre-adjust velocity): 28 frames standing, Up+B 15, Up+Left+B 4, Up+B 29 (the last 7 slide right along the wall: pre-velocity (0,-2), velocity (+1,0)) through the door tile $2935 (the opened-door list $7F:1CC8 = 2935, as the capture's), Down 1, Down+B 13, Down+Left+B 11, Left+B until the patrolling Diablos (obj 1E, 704..752 and back, a 240-frame period from the load) meets the lead on the 37th step left, as in the ring. The 28 frames are the patrol's phase: after 26 or 27 it meets the lead a step early, after 30 a step late; 28 and 29 meet it on the 37th, 28 nearest the capture (1454 bytes of WRAM apart, 29: 2062). The battle positions ($1D0C/$1D23 3F 7E AE / 80 7C 80) are then the capture's. Not reached: the entrance ladder's per-enemy tile row $924D (32.. here, 36.. on the capture: C1/3639-3657 reads ROM E4 at $5DF1 + $1C99 + $A9) and the capture's real-time battle phase -- the capture predates the rule (2026-10-01), whose cartridge does not replay its own recorded fight either (see fx_party3_field).
